Oh, and Derrick Henry will look to run all over his former team in the Tennessee Titans . That's a must-watch revenge game. Let's discuss some anytime touchdown bets. These have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Last week, we hit on Tee Higgins at +175 and tight end Harold Fannin Jr . at +235. Let's see what we have cooking up for Week 4. Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider. These will not be predictable choices like a Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a tight end who looked incredible last week in his 2026 debut. Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook. 1. Raiders TE Brock Bowers (+160) The Las Vegas Raiders have a massive matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs this week. The Raiders are off to a surprising 3-0 start, although we can't ignore the fact that they've played the easiest strength of schedule in the NFL up to this point, as their first three opponents have won one game combined. Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers made his season debut last week against the New Orleans Saints , and he looked magnificent. He caught a game-high 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown in a 35-27 win, and will be important if the Raiders want to score an upset victory over their rivals. With how good Bowers looked last week, I'll sprinkle on him again in this spot as Kirk Cousins ' new clear-cut "WR1." 2. Bills RB James Cook (-140) James Cook of the Buffalo Bills is one of the best running backs in the NFL, and he's on a bit of a heater right now. He rushed 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 vs. the Detroit Lions , and then 24 times for 154 yards and another touchdown last week against the Los Angeles Chargers . Now, the flailing New England Patriots come to town, and they are missing two important defenders in Christian Barmore and Christian Gonzalez . They lost by 29 points to the Jacksonville Jaguars last week, and I'm sure Joe Brady and the Bills want to do something similar to the team that won their division last year. A -140 price isn't value, but I can tell you I was surprised by this listing. 3. Vikings RB Aaron Jones (-160) Like James Cook, this line doesn't offer much value. But consider that the Miami Dolphins have allowed six touchdowns to running backs through three games. The Minnesota Vikings are favored by double-digits over Miami, which makes sense because the Dolphins just lost De'Von Achane for the year, while Brian Flores is going to look to DESTROY his former team from a defensive standpoint. That means Aaron Jones is going to get plenty of touches. He hasn't scored since Week 1, but will in Week 4. 4. Jets RB Braelon Allen (+115) I was a fan of Braelon Allen in the 2024 draft process because he's big at 6-foot-1, 235 pounds, and was the youngest player in the entire class. He actually racked up 482 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns as a rookie, but an injury held him to four games played last year. Now, he's making his third career start with Breece Hall sidelined by a quad injury. When the New York Jets get in the red zone against the Chicago Bears , Frank Reich is going to call his number. 5. Saints RB Alvin Kamara (+135) (Monday) This game is on Monday night, but I had to mention it. The Saints are hosting the Atlanta Falcons in the 20th anniversary of the "Rebirth Game," where the Saints returned to the Superdome for the first time following Hurricane Katrina. The legendary Steve Gleason blocked a punt on the opening drive of the game, which set the tone for an emotional 23-3 Saints victory. I can't imagine what the environment will be like on Monday night. Travis Etienne is out with a hamstring injury, opening the door for franchise legend Alvin Kamara . He's not as productive as he used to be, but it makes too much sense for him to score in this game. Bonus: Ravens RB Derrick Henry 2 TDs (+250) Derrick Henry faces the team that selected him No. 45 overall in the 2016 NFL Draft this Sunday. Henry and the Titans didn't have some dramatic breakup, but Henry wanted to win football games and the Titans were about to suffer an embarrassing fall to the bottom of the league, so a mutual parting of ways made sense. It used to be a debate if Henry was a future Hall of Famer. Not anymore. The ageless wonder leads the NFL with 3,817 rushing yards and 38 rushing touchdowns since signing with the Baltimore Ravens in 2024. Those are more rushing yards and more rushing touchdowns than the entire Titans offense since he left. Derrick Henry to find the end zone at -210 is probably a parlay leg, but what about two touchdowns at +250? He's averaging two touchdowns a game this year as it is! However, the Rams, with two Ls, might be slightly more desperate than Philadelphia. And then over in the AFC, we've got Patrick Mahomes playing like he's back to his old form and Kirk Cousins lighting up the scoreboard. Let's dive into how I'm wagering on the weekend. Rams @ Eagles Simply put, I don’t think the Eagles are very good right now, and it might not be their year. I did not like the hiring of a first-time offensive coordinator to pair with Jalen Hurts and the results so far are on par with what I expected — a disjointed offense that ranks 17th in offensive DVOA. Hurts is ranked 27th in EPA per play. The Eagles' offensive line hasn’t been its usual self and I think the play-calling hasn’t made much sense. The Rams' defense is fourth in DVOA this season and should be able to disrupt the Eagles' offense in a meaningful way this Sunday. On the other side is an L.A. offense that has shown brilliant moments this season, while also displaying some weaknesses. Last week against the Broncos, the Rams started fast on offense and then disappeared, punctuated by a Matthew Stafford pick-six. Matthew Stafford will try to lead the Rams over the Eagles in NFL Week 4. (Getty Images) The possible return of Puka Nacua will help the Rams' passing attack. On paper, the Rams' offensive line should struggle in this game, but the Eagles' defensive line has been underwhelming. PFF has the Eagles' pass rush ranked 27th in the NFL and the tackling is ranked at about that level, too. The Rams are 1-2, and after blowing that game on Sunday, they need to win this weekend. You shouldn’t just solely wager on teams because they need to win, but that’s part of the equation for me. I get a better quarterback and a better coach who’s playing better football. Schwartz's Pick: Rams -3 Chiefs @ Raiders The Chiefs are 3-0 and playing better football on offense than they have in years. Mahomes looks completely healthy after missing the end of the season with an ACL injury. It was assumed Mahomes would be less mobile, but he’s been moving around the pocket and down the field like usual. In the Chiefs' first game against an excellent Broncos defense, he rushed for 23 yards. In Week 2 against the Colts, he rushed for 17 yards in an overtime win. Patrick Mahomes seems to have found his groove again. (Getty Images) Last week, Mahomes only rush attempt was when he kneeled. The Chiefs' offensive line has played fine this season, but the pass protection has been a concern. Now this group has to play Maxx Crosby and that’s a recipe for pressure on Mahomes. When Mahomes feels pressure or understands it might be a game featuring pressure, he tends to run the ball more often. Kansas City might also need to keep up with the Raiders' scoring output if Cousins continues to put up points for the Raiders. That will lead to a more aggressive Mahomes rushing the football. Derrick Henry is looking to run wild against his former team in the Tennessee Titans; the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders battle from London; and Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams look to get back on track vs. the Philadelphia Eagles . This season has been pretty unpredictable so far. Four teams enter Week 4 tied for the best record in their division after last-place finishes in 2025: The Las Vegas Raiders , Cleveland Browns , New York Giants and the New Orleans Saints . Which one of these teams could be a legitimate sleeper? And when could we see J.J. McCarthy take over at quarterback in New York? Below, CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Sept. 29 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Advanced data courtesy of CBS Sports Research Indianapolis Colts (-3.5) vs. Washington Commanders (London) Dajani (Colts -3.5): I think this matchup is about which defense stinks less. The Colts rank worst in total defense (417.3) and third-worst in scoring defense (30.3). The Commanders rank second-worst in scoring defense (30.7) and have allowed the highest opponent passer rating (124.4) and most passing touchdowns (11) this year. Marcus Mariota has definitely brought some magic to the lineup, as evidenced by last week's upset of the Seattle Seahawks , but I would argue the Colts are the better team. Do you remember the last time the Colts played overseas? They defeated the Atlanta Falcons in overtime thanks to a ridiculous performance from Jonathan Taylor . The star running back rushed 32 times for 244 yards and three touchdowns, while also adding 42 yards as a receiver. He's already up to 325 total yards and four touchdowns through three weeks. I expect him to show out on Sunday for our friends across the pond. … Prediction: Colts 27, Commanders 21 Dubin (Commanders +3.5): Marcus Mariota is a competent enough backup quarterback to keep this game close. He just went and beat the Seahawks, after all, and the Colts have a much friendlier defense. He should be able to keep the chains moving. I'm just not sure that'll be enough for the Commanders to actually win the game this time around. I think this is a big Jonathan Taylor game, even if Washington has been good on the ground so far and allowed just 44 rushing yards last week against Seattle. Plus. Washington's pass defense should give Daniel Jones and Co. a chance for their best game to date. … Prediction: Colts 23, Commanders 20 Jacksonville Jaguars at Cincinnati Bengals (-2.5) Dajani (Bengals -2.5): The Jacksonville Jaguars have been red-hot and just defeated the New England Patriots by a whopping 29 points. As for the Bengals, they just lost to Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers in a thrilling game. We thought the Cincy defense was reborn, only for Rodgers and Co. to drop 30 points on them. This is going to be a popular "upset" pick this week, but I'm actually going to take the Bengals. They are back at home after two road games and have covered the spread in six straight non-divisional contests. This Jaguars team isn't perfect, and you saw some issues during their Week 2 loss to the Denver Broncos . The offensive line could struggle with Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen , while this secondary will have their hands full with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . Don't overlook the fact that Joe Burrow is 3-0 vs. Trevor Lawrence dating back to the 2019 College Football Playoff Title game. … Prediction: Bengals 24, Jaguars 20 Dubin (Jaguars +2.5): I hate to be the guy that takes what Dajani described as the popular upset pick right after he called people out for it, but I'm going to do just that. The Jaguars should be 3-0 right now, but they fell apart in the second half against the Broncos in Week 2. The offense is firing on all cylinders. The defense has forced six turnovers in three games. Cincinnati's defensive improvement looked like a mirage in Week 3 against the Steelers and may have just been a function of playing dysfunctional offenses in the Buccaneers and the Nico Collins-less Texans . I think Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins can put up some points here, but I like the Jags to score even more. … Prediction: Jaguars 30, Bengals 27 Los Angeles Rams (-3) at Philadelphia Eagles Dajani (Rams -3): The Eagles' loss to the Chicago Bears may stay with me forever. We had a 38-year-old quarterback dicing up a Super Bowl-caliber defense, as Ben Johnson put Vic Fangio in a proverbial chokehold on national television. Then, we had a former Super Bowl MVP quarterback looking completely lost. All that to say, how am I supposed to back Philly in this spot against an angry team that just lost in primetime? If we are being honest with ourselves, the Eagles haven't looked very good at all this year. They were hardly dominant in the Week 1 victory over the Commanders or Week 2 win against the Titans. Philly is the only team that hasn't scored in the first quarter this season, and the defense is still waiting to force that first takeaway. The Eagles haven't even covered the spread this season, so I'll take the visiting Rams to get back on track. … Prediction: Rams 26, Eagles 20 Dubin (Rams -3): The Rams have looked like the Rams we expected for six quarters this season, and very much like a different team for the other six quarters. Meanwhile, the Eagles have looked exactly like the Eagles we expected for eight quarters and like a disaster for four. How does that all net out? I think it nets out with Matthew Stafford having some success through the air against a somewhat surprisingly friendly Eagles pass defense that isn't getting as much pressure as you'd expect, and with Jalen Hurts and Co. continuing their stilted start to the season. … Prediction: Rams 24, Eagles 20 Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans (-2.5) Dajani (Texans -2.5): I've given the Texans the benefit of the doubt for an entire month with nothing to show for it. I can no longer wait for C.J. Stroud to get the offense off the ground or for the defense to become good again. With that said, there is one big reason why the Texans will get their first win this season, and that's Nico Collins . He's missed the past two games with a hamstring injury, but should return this week to face one of the worst defenses in the NFL. C.J. Stroud averages 10.7 yards per attempt when targeting Collins. That number drops to 7.7 when he targets any other receiver. In the one game Collins played in this season, he caught seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown while Houston came one play away from defeating the Buffalo Bills … Prediction: Texans 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (Texans -2.5): The Cowboys need their offense to be perfect in order to win games. Their defense once again seems like it's that bad, and it is also hemorrhaging players at linebacker and in the secondary. Offenses, generally, cannot be perfect against the Texans' defense. Houston should also be getting Nico Collins back here, so I think the Texans can actually move the ball for a change. … Prediction: Texans 24, Cowboys 21 Denver Broncos at San Francisco 49ers (-3) Dajani (Broncos +3): Maybe I'm the Broncos expert? When Denver was down 16-0 to the Rams last Sunday night, I was telling everyone not to go to bed because the game was not over. Sure enough, the Broncos bucked back. Denver has the most comeback wins (14), second-half comebacks (11), fourth-quarter comebacks (7) and 14-point comebacks (3) over the past two seasons. I'm leaning toward the Broncos again in this spot because of the San Francisco 49ers ' injuries. Nick Bosa is going to miss some time with knee/calf issues, wide receiver Mike Evans injured his rib, linebacker Dre Greenlaw sat out of practice Wednesday with a quad injury and we'll see what the status of left tackle Trent Williams is later in the week. Denver is 5-1 straight up in its last six games as an underdog, and Bo Nix is 10-0 in his past 10 games vs. NFC opponents. … Prediction: Broncos 24, 49ers 23 Dubin (49ers -3): San Francisco is merrily rolling right along with the best offense in the NFL through the first three weeks despite pass-catchers dropping like flies. Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are just that good, I suppose. The Broncos have looked either terrible or amazing so far this year, and I just don't think that type of thing is enough to hang with the 49ers in their current form. … Prediction: 49ers 24, Broncos 16 Detroit Lions (-3.5) at Carolina Panthers (SNF) Dajani ( Lions -3.5): I'm a bit partial to the Lions despite their horrific defense. We got the cover last week vs. the New York Jets , but it was quite a sweat. I'm taking the Lions this week because of the Panthers' injury situation. They will not have their two starting cornerbacks on the field in Jaycee Horn or Mike Jackson . Keep in mind this Panthers defense is already statistically one of the worst in the NFL and had 552 total yards and 59 points dropped on them in their last home game. The Lions are simply going to outscore the Panthers in primetime, and I think we could be looking at a blowout. The Lions are 11-0 SU and 9-1-1 ATS in primetime games as favorites under Dan Campbell. Get ready for some points. … Prediction: Lions 35, Panthers 21 Dubin (Lions -3.5): Lions games have turned into track meets so far this season, with Detroit scoring at least 30 points in every game. With the Panthers likely down their top two cornerbacks, this week is set up for them to go off yet again. We might even see Jameson Williams really pop off for the first time this year. And we know both Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown will be productive. Bryce Young is leading the NFL in passing yards, but he might not have Jalen Coker here, so the Panthers might not have quite enough to compete here, even given how bad the Lions' defense is. … Prediction: Lions 34, Panthers 24 Atlanta Falcons at New Orleans Saints (-3) (MNF) Dajani (Saints -3): I would rather have the moneyline here, but I'll ride with the Saints. After all, this is the 20th anniversary of the team's return to the Superdome following Hurricane Katrina. I can't even begin to imagine what the stadium is going to feel like Monday night. The Falcons registered that incredible victory against the Green Bay Packers last Thursday, but I almost think that game showed us more about the Packers than it did the Falcons. Atlanta is clearly better with Michael Penix Jr . under center, but it would be tragic if the Saints lost this game given the celebration. … Prediction: Saints 28, Falcons 20 Dubin (Push): The Falcons looked much improved last week against the Packers, thanks in large part to the return of Michael Penix Jr. They hadn't even entered the red zone through the first two weeks of the season, then dropped 35 points on the Packers in Week 2. The Saints, meanwhile, could conceivably be 3-0 right now if not for backbreaking turnovers. They have two one-possession losses, both in games where they turned it over at least three times. If they can avoid giving the ball to the Falcons, I think they can win a close one here. … Prediction: Saints 23, Falcons 20 Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5) at Cleveland Browns (TNF) Dajani ( Steelers -2.5): Ready for a crazy stat? The Steelers have lost seven straight road games against the Browns when not starting Ben Roethlisberger at quarterback. The last non-Roethlisberger Steelers quarterback to win in Cleveland was Tommy Maddox in 2003! Maybe it takes a Hall of Famer like Aaron Rodgers to break that streak, even if he lost to Shedeur Sanders in Cleveland last year. The Steelers are Jekyll and Hyde to me. They registered one of the worst offensive performances I've ever seen in Week 2, only to drop 30 points and 411(!) total yards on the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3! So, which Steelers team are we going to see on Thursday? I'm not 100% sure, but I will say that the Browns' 2-1 start is overrated. This offense ranks bottom five in yards per game (266.0), third down percentage (30.6%) and red zone TD percentage (37.5%) this season, and probably should have blown out the Carolina Panthers last Sunday … Prediction: Steelers 21, Browns 17 Dubin (Steelers -2.5): The Browns have won each of their last two games with late scores. However, they have been out-gained in each game this season and have yet to record more than 17 first downs in a given game. I don't have any confidence that their offense can consistently move the ball against Pittsburgh's defense. I don't have much more confidence in Pittsburgh's offense, which did nothing in its first two games before exploding against the Bengals this past week, but I do have somewhat more confidence in it than in Cleveland's. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 14 Add CBS Sports on Google Join the Conversation comments Around the Web Promoted by Taboola Now Playing Share Share Video Link copied! Here's where I'm putting my money. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Steelers @ Browns Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to push the ball down the field more this year than the team did last year with Aaron Rodgers, and he has been true to his word so far. Rodgers’ average depth of target has been over 10 yards in two of the three games so far, including in a 30-27 win last week. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 Colts @ Commanders Don’t forget to set your alarms for this one, as we get our first 9:30 am ET kickoff of the season in London come Sunday. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Hill's Pick: Commanders +3.5 Patriots @ Bills It has not been pretty for the defending AFC champions, but it’s often a good idea to ignore the last thing you saw in the NFL to avoid overreacting. The Patriots will already be 3.5 games out of first place in the AFC East with a loss. They are desperate and getting 6.5 points. I’l bet on them to bounce back. Hill's Pick: Patriots +6.5 Titans @ Ravens If the Titans aren’t the worst team in the NFL, they’re pretty close to it. At 0-3, their offense has been anemic, and I don’t expect it to improve this week in Baltimore. Hill's Pick: Titans Under 15.5 Jaguars @ Bengals The quarterbacks for this game are familiar with each other. Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow were picked first overall, respectively, in back-to-back years (2020 and 2021), and also played against each other in the 2019 college football national title game. The Jaguars look like a contender and could easily be 3-0. In a toss-up game, I’ll take the points. Hill's Pick: Jaguars +2.5 Rams @ Eagles Panic time could officially hit the Rams if they lose again this week and fall to 1-3. The Eagles have had their number recently, winning all four meetings since the start of the 2023 season, and winning in Philadelphia isn’t easy, especially considering the onerous travel the Rams have endured already this season. Hill's Pick: Eagles +3 Cardinals @ Giants The Giants are 2-1, but their offense has looked suspect since quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury. With the total set at 44.5, I think we get a 23-20 type of game. I will go Under here considering the Giants' lackluster offense. Hill's Pick: Under 44.5 Cowboys @ Texans The Cowboys’ defense was expected to be improved in 2026 after being dreadful in 2025, but we have yet to see that play out. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 Jets @ Bears The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. Hill's Pick: Jets +3.5 Packers @ Buccaneers Two desperate teams facing off here with each in dire need of a win. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his first career start for the Buccaneers, and I expect points to be hard to come by. Hill's Pick: Under 38.5 Dolphins @ Vikings The Vikings look to improve to 4-0 and are heavy favorites to do so against the hapless Dolphins. While it’s been an impressive start for the Vikings, they have struggled mightily on offense, and aren’t well-equipped to exploit the Dolphins’ weak secondary. Star wide receiver Justin Jefferson might be sidelined for this one, and 10.5 points is a lot to lay for a struggling Vikings offense. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +10.5 Chiefs @ Raiders Raiders’ tight end Brock Bowers is one of the best, and perhaps, still one of the most underrated players in the league. Coming off of 13 targets, 10 catches and 116 yards in his season debut, expect another big game from Bowers. Hill's Pick: Brock Bowers Over 76.5 Receiving Yards Chargers @ Seahawks The Chargers look broken offensively and could not defeat the Bills last week despite their defense forcing five turnovers. I don’t look for them to do much offensively on the road, in a hostile environment against an angry Seahawks defense coming off an upset loss to the Commanders. Hill's Pick: Chargers Under 17.5 Broncos @ 49ers The 49ers are undefeated and have been ultra impressive so far, but as usual, the injuries are starting to pile up. In what should be a close game, I’ll take the Broncos to keep it close. Hill's Pick: Broncos +3 Lions @ Panthers The Lions have played three games and they’ve all gone Over. With an elite offense and very suspect defense, I like another Lions Over. Hill's Pick: Over 51.5 Falcons @ Saints The Saints gave up over 100 yards rushing last week and now face perhaps the most dynamic running back in the NFL. Look for Bijan Robinson to have another big game on the ground. More NFL Betting Advice NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet Expert NFL Game Picks NFL Betting Strategy Best +EV NFL Picks Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App >> Best Week 2 NFL Thursday Night Football Player Props: Lions vs. Bills (Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook ) Jameson Williams 60+ Yards ( -112 ) We suggested the receiving yards for Jameson Williams earlier in the week to get a jump on some lower totals. That line opened at 50+ and has now ballooned to 60+, with the possibility of ascending a bit further. Hopefully you were able to get in when the total was between 50 and 55 yards. A little extra work needs to get done to clear the 60+ threshold tonight. However, the young receiver could be in a very favorable spot to do so in a projected high-scoring affair. Williams caught four passes for 45 yards in Week 1 for the Lions. We expect the young receiver to see a few more targets this evening. The total for this contest is at 54. Which means both teams are set to go off offensively, and Williams could very well be the beneficiary in that type of game script. Buffalo allowed over 375 passing yards on 35 completions to New Orleans on Sunday. Detroit clearly has a more prolific offense than New Orleans. Anywhere near 300 yards passing should result in 60+ receiving yards for Williams. Jahmyr Gibbs 5+ Rushing Yards Every Quarter ( -130 ) This is one you have to dig for. Luckily, we have done the work for you. When you want to make a game a little more interesting beyond your standard bets and props, take a look at some of the game props. A favorite prop I use regularly is both teams to rush for a touchdown when I'm looking for a positive return, and both teams to throw a touchdown when I'm looking for something to cap off a parlay. The tale of the tape should tell you where and when to utilize these props for the maximum success. Taking a high-volume player to record at least five yards every quarter in what is currently the highest total on the board will always be a play that profits you in the long run. That's especially true when the player rushed the ball on 29 plays in the team’s first game. Jahmyr Gibbs finished with 156 yards on the ground and 5.4 yards per carry last week. While a repeat of 29 touches sounds ambitious, the five-yards-per-carry mark should be enough for Gibbs to rush for at least five yards in every quarter. The young running back accounted for 29 of the Lions’ 33 rushing attempts in Week 1. Both Teams to Score 1+ Rushing Touchdown ( -130 ) As previously mentioned, this is a prop bet that is normally a plus return. Given the 54-point total, the oddsmakers are taxing us. The juice at -130 is not ideal. However, we don't want to miss out on what could be one of the most straightforward options tonight. Not only do we have two of the highest-usage running backs facing off tonight, but Josh Allen also rushed for two touchdowns on Sunday. This play is even more successful when there are two quarterbacks who can score with their legs. Josh Allen and Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for two touchdowns each in their Week 1 matchups. Gibbs is without a doubt the goal-line option for Detroit. Whereas, in Buffalo, we have two very viable options that can rush for a touchdown. The projected points scored by each team are between 24 and 30 points. If that's the case, it's more than likely to include a rushing touchdown from both teams. James Cook First Quarter: 1+ Receptions ( +109 ) James Cook may be looked upon early in this contest considering Detroit's ability to rush the pass. If Josh Allen needs a quick outlet to an open receiver after the defense breaks through, Cook or Dalton Kincaid make the most sense. Kincaid offers a positive return on investment (ROI) on two catches. So, we are going to take the option out of the backfield to catch at least one pass in the first quarter. Cook caught three passes for 12 yards in Buffalo's first contest against Houston. Detroit is equally as active on the pass rush, which should lead to an early reception for Cook. The Lions successfully dropped the quarterback on four plays against the Texans on Sunday - led by Aidan Hutchinson, who recorded two sacks in the contest. Houston running back David Montgomery caught three passes against Detroit, while Woody Marks also recorded one reception. We're back with the same crew that includes analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford . Last season, Gagnon and Hanford led the group at 143-127-2 for the season. Moton finished third at 139-131-2. Our panel will use the same format as last year, sharing all their picks and challenging each other with opposing views on every game unless there's a unanimous selection. We'll also keep track of lone-wolf picks, which were 32-29-1 last year. Now, let's look ahead to the Week 1 slate, which starts Wednesday with the Super Bowl LX rematch and a lone-wolf pick right off the top. Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Sept. 9, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings . New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks 1 of 16 AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba FanDuel Line: Seahawks (-3.5) Knox: Seahawks (-3.5) I don't think the Super Bowl LX rematch will be as one-sided as last year's championship game. However, I do believe Seattle's defensive front can prevent Drake Maye and the Patriots from finding an offensive rhythm once again. With home-field advantage playing a factor, Seattle should win by more than a field goal and walk away with a 1-0 record. Moton: Patriots (+3.5) It's understandable that the panel leaned heavily toward the Seahawks, given Seattle's dominant 29-13 victory over New England in Super Bowl LX seven months ago. Since then, the Seahawks have lost key parts of that team and coaching staff. Former Seahawks offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak is now the head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders. Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker, who led Seattle's backfield with 1,027 yards and five touchdowns, signed with the Kansas City Chiefs. The Seahawks also lost cornerback Riq Woolen and safety Coby Bryant in free agency. Meanwhile, the Patriots added wideouts A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Running back TreVeyon Henderson won't play because of an ankle injury, though Rhamondre Stevenson has handled a workhorse role in the past. New England covers the 3.5-point spread. Predictions Patriots: Moton Seahawks: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams (in Australia) 2 of 16 AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford FanDuel Line: Rams (-3.5) Hanford: Rams (-3.5) There's no team entering the season with bigger hype than the Rams, and I'm buying it. While you could argue that their travel plans and a 49ers team that's probably more overlooked than it should be entering the season is a recipe for an upset, I think the Rams will show right away why they're the Super Bowl favorites. L.A. wins by a touchdown behind a dominant defensive performance. O'Donnell: 49ers (+3.5) Both teams have been major offseason headline generators: the Rams for building a super team headlined by the Myles Garrett trade and return of Aaron Donald; and the 49ers for what boils down to a lot of negativity headlined by injuries. In fact, while almost all the focus has been on George Kittle's potential return in Week 1, we don't actually know if Christian McCaffrey will be fit to play, and conventional wisdom would be to back the favorites. But these two teams traveled a long, long way to play a football game, and I'd rather take the points against a familiar foe in an unfamiliar setting regardless of who is on the field. Predictions 49ers: Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell Rams: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Sobleski Buffalo Bills at Houston Texans 3 of 16 AP Photo/David J. Phillip Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud FanDuel Line: Bills (-1.5) Davenport: Bills (-1.5) Laying points on the road against arguably the NFL's best defense is starting the season with some anxiety. But I have that much more anxiety about C.J. Stroud after how he finished last season—Josh Allen leads the Bills to a close win on one of Week 1's better games. Gagnon: Texans (+1.5) Week 1 is a lot of gut, and I have a feeling the Houston defense will be extremely prepared for Buffalo in the Texans' home opener. That was certainly the case when they beat the Bills at this very site in November 2025. The Bills are an excellent team, but this is a tough spot for their new coach. Predictions Bills: Davenport Texans: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski TOP NEWS New NFL Power Rankings 📊 Bleacher Report 2h Cam Jordan Rips into Saints Bleacher Report 1h The Robinsons POUND the Rock 🪨 Bleacher Report 10h Chicago Bears at Carolina Panthers 4 of 16 AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams FanDuel Line: Bears (-2.5) Moton: Bears (-2.5) The Bears enter this matchup with a shaky secondary. Safety Coby Bryant underwent knee surgery and will miss a few months of action. Slot cornerback Kyler Gordon is on the physically unable to perform list with a calf injury. However, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young hasn't shown the ability to exploit opposing pass defenses' weaknesses, averaging just 180.2 passing yards per game over his three-year career. Bears go on the road with their ascending offense and win by at least a field goal. Sobleski: Bears (-2.5) The Carolina Panthers finished among the bottom six in total offense last season. The organization added next-to-nothing to improve the unit. If anything, the group might be worse since both offensive tackle spots remain a serious concern. Conversely, the Chicago Bears are explosive enough offensively to easily cover this spread. Predictions Bears: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski Cleveland Browns at Jacksonville Jaguars 5 of 16 AP Photo/Gary McCullough Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence FanDuel Line: Jaguars (-7.5) Gagnon: Jaguars (-7.5) I think the Browns could have some surprisingly nice moments this season, but this ain't the spot. Cleveland is, at the very least, a work in progress as a new core and coaching staff settle in. The Jaguars, on the other hand, are a well-oiled machine on a strong trajectory following a superb second half to the 2025 campaign. I expect them to keep rolling in their home opener. Sobleski: Browns (+7.5) Despite every expectation of the Cleveland Browns' offense imploding thanks to questionable quarterback setup, Todd Monken's squad gets the benefit of the doubt in the head coach's debut because of its defense. Myles Garrett might be gone, but this unit still has playmakers at all three levels to slow the Jaguars and make the contest interesting. Predictions Browns: Hanford, Knox, Sobleski Jaguars: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell Atlanta Falcons at Pittsburgh Steelers 6 of 16 AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers FanDuel Line: Steelers (-3.5) Gagnon: Falcons (+3.5) I don't trust the Steelers, and I hate that hook for them. It's really that simple. These teams are closer to being evenly matched than many might believe, and the Steelers were far from impressive at home in 2025. The Falcons didn't lose by more than a field goal in regulation in any of their last six road games last season. They should keep this game tight. Hanford: Steelers (-3.5) The jury is out on Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy's reunion in Pittsburgh and the impact it will have on a stagnant Steelers offense, but I just don't see the "winner" of the NFL's least inspiring QB battle, Tua Tagovailoa, doing serious damage to the Steelers defense. I expect this game to be ugly, like most Steelers games, but Tagovailoa makes one too many mistakes as Pittsburgh improves to 6-1 ATS in its last seven games against Atlanta. Predictions Falcons: Gagnon Steelers: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski New York Jets at Tennessee Titans 7 of 16 AP Photo/George Walker IV Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward FanDuel Line: Titans (-1.5) Davenport: Jets (+1.5) Fans who watch this entire game should receive some sort of reparations from the NFL. Neither offense in this slopfest can be trusted even a little, but for my money the Jets are slightly better defensively. First team to 13 points wins! Knox: Titans (-1.5) I'm inclined to believe it when I see it with Robert Saleh, Cam Ward, and the Titans. However, I believe they at least have the potential to turn things around quickly. The Jets? Not so much. I believe that New York is playing for 2027 and beyond. I don't envision Tennessee running away with this one, but I don't see the Jets winning on the road, and this is awfully close to a pick'em. Predictions Jets: Davenport Titans: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski New Orleans Saints at Detroit Lions 8 of 16 AP Photo/Caroline Brehman New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough FanDuel Line: Lions (-7) Hanford: Saints (+7) The Saints closed last season red hot, and while some of that may be fool's gold, I think they'll keep this one within a touchdown. I expect Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs and Co. to have success against the Saints' defense, but I don't trust the Lions' secondary to give Tyler Shough major issues. Lions win by six in a high-scoring game. O'Donnell: Lions (-7) Hey, the Saints are going to be feisty, and the panel is just about split on the Lions giving this many points for good reason. Missing the playoffs a year ago should be gnawing at Dan Campbell's group, though. Detroit scored an average of 32-plus points per game at home last season — a full touchdown more than on the road. Can the Saints go toe-to-toe in a shootout with the Lions in Detroit? Maybe, but I'll back a first-week barrage from the stronger offensive unit as the Lions look to set the tone for a rebound campaign. Predictions Saints: Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski Lions: Davenport, Gagnon, O'Donnell Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals 9 of 16 AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow FanDuel Line: Bengals (-3.5) Knox: Buccaneers (+3.5) If Joe Burrow can stay healthy, Cincinnati's new-look defense should make the Bengals legitimate AFC contenders. However, the Bengals have been notorious for slow starts under Zac Taylor. I can't envision them winning big against a Buccaneers team that can play the underdog card after missing the playoffs in 2025. Sobleski: Bengals (-3.5) Joe Burrow and Co. should hit the ground running. Can the Tampa Bay Buccaneers do the same without Mike Evans on the roster? Obviously, quarterback Baker Mayfield has other weapons in Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan. However, the Cincinnati Bengals still have an advantage in offensive firepower with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, who were both back at practice this week. Predictions Buccaneers: Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell Bengals: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, Sobleski Baltimore Ravens at Indianapolis Colts 10 of 16 AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson FanDuel Line: Ravens (-3.5) Hanford: Ravens (-3.5) Backing this many favorites at 3.5 makes me antsy, but I think the Ravens will be too much for the Colts here. I'm not sold on the Ravens overall this season, but I think their improved defense under Jesse Minter, with the addition of Trey Hendrickson, should give them enough punch to make life very difficult for Daniel Jones. Lamar Jackson has to get back on track as a passer this season, but I think he makes enough plays to put Baltimore over the top. Sobleski: Colts (+3.5) Interestingly, the Indianapolis Colts' defense has a very specific matchup in its favor, with the defensive tackle duo of DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart facing two brand-new starters along the Baltimore Ravens' offensive line. Thus, the Colts could control the line of scrimmage to make life difficult on quarterback Lamar Jackson and running back Derrick Henry. Offensively, Indianapolis should have all of its pieces back in place to get off to a hot start, as it did last season. Predictions Ravens: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton Colts: Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles 11 of 16 AP Photo/Daniel Kucin Jr. Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels FanDuel Line: Eagles (-5.5) Hanford: Eagles (-5.5) The Eagles have a lot of questions to answer on the offensive side of the ball in Week 1, but I'm just not buying the Commanders yet. Jayden Daniels is healthy, which will help, but the weapons around him leave some to be desired, and the absence of star LT Laremy Tunsil will loom large against an Eagles defense that loves to get after the quarterback. I'm not sure Jalen Hurts silences the critics in Week 1, but I do think the Eagles have enough juice in the run game and on defense to control the game and win by a touchdown. Moton: Commanders (+5.5) This is a divisional matchup, and both quarterbacks are learning new offenses. Expect both teams to be inefficient in a game of missed opportunities, while both defenses capitalize on miscues with takeaways. Philadelphia also lost some offensive explosiveness when it traded three-time Pro Bowl receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots. On the ground, running back Saquon Barkley helps the Eagles grind out a close victory by a margin short of a touchdown. Predictions Commanders: Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski Eagles: Davenport, Hanford Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings 12 of 16 AP Photo/Abbie Parr Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson FanDuel Line: Vikings (-1.5) Davenport: Packers (+1.5) Neither of these teams are especially easy to trust in the early-going this year—the Vikings have a new quarterback in Kyler Murray and the Packers have significant questions on defense, especially where the pass rush is concerned. I'll take the points—with exactly zero confidence. Gagnon: Vikings (-1.5) I don't know how I feel about the Packers opening the season on the road against a sneaky-good division rival without Josh Jacobs and Micah Parsons. Throw in the unpredictability factor with Kyler Murray, and I think Green Bay is in a tough situation here. Predictions Packers: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell Vikings: Davenport, Sobleski Miami Dolphins at Las Vegas Raiders 13 of 16 AP Photo/John Locher Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty FanDuel Line: Raiders (-3.5) Moton: Raiders (-3.5) According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Las Vegas Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers is expected to miss "a game or two" after undergoing a trim on his meniscus. On a positive note from the injury front, head coach Klint Kubiak is optimistic about running back Ashton Jeanty suiting up after he suffered an ankle injury during practice on August 23. Without Bowers, expect the Raiders to feature Jeanty (if healthy) and rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. on the ground, which should be enough to control time of possession. The Miami Dolphins offense may not see much time on the field. Although the Raiders have an unproven secondary, with rookie second-rounder Treydan Stukes likely to play at safety and second-year pro Darien Porter at the No. 2 cornerback spot, quarterback Kirk Cousins is more equipped to dice up a shaky pass defense than Malik Willis. O'Donnell: Dolphins (+3.5) Woof. Two organizations in complete rebuild mode. Two new starting quarterbacks under new coaching staffs. Just give me the points in this one, and I'll figure out what to do with these two for the rest of the season after Week 1. Predictions Dolphins: Hanford, O'Donnell Raiders: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton, Sobleski Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Chargers 14 of 16 AP Photo/Gregory Bull Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert FanDuel Line: Chargers (-9.5) Davenport: Cardinals (+9.5) To be clear, the Arizona Cardinals have about as much chance of winning this game as I do of winning an Academy Award. But Arizona has talent on offense and showed it can move the ball last season—Jacoby Brissett will lead a garbage-time touchdown drive late and the Redbirds will sneak in the back door for the cover. Moton: Chargers (-9.5) Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has been teammates with his top pass-catchers for multiple years, and the team added tight end David Njoku, who has 384 receptions for 4,062 yards and 34 touchdowns in his nine-year career. With newly established offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel calling the plays, the Chargers could score in flurries against the Cardinals, who retained defensive coordinator Nick Rallis after his unit gave up the fourth-most points last season. Predictions Cardinals: Davenport, Hanford Chargers: Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski Dallas Cowboys at New York Giants 15 of 16 AP Photo/Rick Scuteri Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott FanDuel Line: Cowboys (-2.5) Knox: Cowboys (-2.5) Will the Giants be better under new head coach John Harbaugh? Yes. Are they prepared to keep pace with a team that has one of the NFL's top offenses and a vastly improved defense? At this point in the season, I don't believe so. Week 1 divisional matchups can be unpredictable, and I won't be shocked if the Giants steal this one. I think it's far more likely that Dallas makes one or two defensive plays that it wouldn't have made a year ago to preserve a one-score victory. O'Donnell: Giants (+2.5) The Cowboys are the better team on paper, and the Giants' secondary will have a hard time defending CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens even if Big Blue is getting to Dak Prescott. But if a new coaching staff and the return of two injured star players to the lineup (Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers), on top of two rookie first-round picks starting in their debuts (Arvell Reese and Francis Mauigoa), at home on Sunday Night Football against a bitter rival, isn't enough to get a team up, then what in the gorydamn hell are we playing this game for? Predictions Cowboys: Davenport, Knox, Moton, Sobleski Giants: Gagnon, Hanford, O'Donnell Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs 16 of 16 AP Photo/Jack Dempsey Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix FanDuel Line: Chiefs (-2.5) Knox: Broncos (+2.5) Winning as the road team in Kansas City is tough, but defense travels, and the Broncos have one of the best in the business. Beyond that, I think it's going to take a few games for Patrick Mahomes to find his groove with whatever post-injury playing style he brings to the 2026 season. The Chiefs will go as Mahomes does, and one or two instances of him hesitating behind the line will sink them against arguably the most well-rounded team in the conference. O'Donnell: Chiefs (-2.5) The Denver defense is going to be a problem for Kansas City, especially with a less than 100% healthy Patrick Mahomes back under center. On paper, the Broncos might be the better all-around team, too. And the Chiefs have lost two of the last three season openers, with the lone victory being a controversial end-of-game call that gave K.C. the victory over Baltimore in 2024. Yeah, all things point to a Broncos cover, if not an outright win. So, I'll ride with the minority and lay these points with the home team covering late. Without further ado, here are three of the best player props for NFL Week 1, including Garrett Wilson, David Montgomery and Omarion Hampton. *]:mx-auto lg:[&>*]:mx-0"> Best NFL Player Prop Bets and Picks for Week 1 David Montgomery Anytime TD (-120) David Montgomery has found a new home in Houston. The Lions’ “Sonic and Knuckles” duo in the backfield was one of the best in the league over the past few years. However, Montgomery was always second fiddle to Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit. He was always productive, especially in the red zone, but now he has the chance to be the RB1 for the Texans. Over the past three seasons, Montgomery has scored 33 touchdowns on the ground, despite being in that backup role. Now, he should get almost all of the touches when Houston is in the scoring area. The Bills had an awful run defense last season. They ranked 31st in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 25th in defensive rushing success rate. This Houston team has struggled with pass protection over the past couple of seasons, so it should try to take advantage of that poor run defense and get the ball to Montgomery whenever possible. David Montgomery should start his Houston tenure with a touchdown. Garrett Wilson 6+ Receptions (-121) During the offseason, new Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich described Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall as the Jets’ “bell cows.” The Jets aren’t a great team, but they know they have two very reliable and dangerous weapons in Wilson and Hall. To make things easy on Geno Smith, Reich will want to scheme ways to get the ball to those two players as often as possible. Wilson dealt with an injury that kept him out for most of last season, but in the first six games of the season when he was fit, Wilson had at least six catches in four of those six games. Geno Smith did not have a good season in Las Vegas, but he had a terrible offensive line and a bad group of skill position players. He might not get back to the guy he was in Seattle, but he should have a much better season with an underrated Jets offensive line protecting him. Smith might have turnover issues, but he is not afraid to let it fly. Since the start of the 2022 season, he ranks fourth in the NFL in pass attempts. This Titans defense is very vulnerable, and Frank Reich should let Geno Smith chuck it early and often in this game. Last season, the Titans ranked 29th in the NFL in defensive EPA/pass and 26th in dropback success rate. This is a good early matchup for Smith to get his feet under him in a Jets uniform (for the second time) and feed his WR1 Garrett Wilson. Omarion Hampton Over 68.5 Rushing Yards (-114) This should be a big season for Omarion Hampton. He only played nine games in his rookie season for the Chargers, but he is set for a huge role in what should be a productive Los Angeles offense. This is a good matchup for him to start the season against the Cardinals. Last season, Arizona ranked 22nd in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 23rd in defensive rushing success rate. That defense has a lot of young, inexperienced pieces and should struggle again this season. The Chargers should feed the ball to Hampton early and often to control the game against Arizona. The Chargers are also big favorites and should lead this game down the stretch. That should lead to a lot of carries for Hampton down the stretch while the Chargers put the game on ice. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Expert Picks 2026 Texans vs Bills Prediction: Houston Texans Moneyline (-105) Based on the Texans’ defensive advantages over a normally strong Bills offense and Buffalo’s lackluster defensive record, my Texans vs Bills prediction is the Texans Moneyline (-105) . When these teams met in Week 12 last year, Buffalo’s offense struggled immensely. For the entire 2025 regular season, Buffalo recorded the following advanced metrics: +0.145 EPA per play and 48.2% success rate, including 50.5% dropback success rate. When the offense went up against Houston: -0.164 EPA per play, 36.9% offensive success rate, 35.6% dropback success rate. Dalton Kincaid missed the game for Buffalo, which in theory should provide a boost. However, Houston also operated without safety Jalen Pitre as a six-point underdog. Davis Mills and Woody Marks combined to move the ball effectively on Buffalo’s defense. The ground game in particular proved very efficient, producing a 54.2% rushing success rate. Comparatively, Houston produced a 35.6% rushing success over the entire season. David Montgomery’s arrival, plus some new pieces along the offensive line, should allow for continued offensive success by the Texans. A change from Mills to C.J. Stroud adds to the ceiling case. Meanwhile, the Texans defense directly mitigates all the strengths of Buffalo’s offense. Buffalo’s normally reliable offensive line faces one of the best pass rushes in the NFL. The Bills ranked fourth in PFF’s pass-blocking grades, but posted their worst grade against Houston. The same occurred when these teams played in Week 5 of the 2024 season. Buffalo averaged a 74.7 offensive pass-blocking grade, which fell to 57.8 against the Texans. More concerning is how the Bills handle new additions to Houston’s defense. Reed Blankenship arrives to play safety after a strong tenure with the Eagles, while Jadeveon Clowney adds depth at edge. Those additions lead me to expect another strong performance from the Texans defense. It leads me to predict a third straight Houston win against Buffalo. Vikings vs Packers Prediction: Minnesota Vikings Moneyline (-120) Based on the Packers’ expected offensive line regression against a blitz-heavy defense and Micah Parsons’ absence, my Vikings vs Packers prediction is the Vikings Moneyline (-120) . It’s difficult to place much stock in either Green Bay-Minnesota matchup last year. Green Bay won 23-6 at home while forcing three defensive turnovers against J.J. McCarthy. The Vikings earned revenge in Week 18, but the 16-3 win came against Clayton Tune. If there’s a unit that should take a step forward from both games last year, it’s the Vikings offense. Presuming Kyler Murray starts, it should open up the passing game against weak Green Bay corners. Late last year, bettors saw the secondary struggle without a coherent pass rush. From Week 13 onward – a sample that includes Parsons – the Packers ranked 28th in EPA per play and 29th in defensive success rate. That includes a Week 15 trip to Denver where Bo Nix shredded Green Bay for over 300 yards and four touchdowns. What really worries me about the Packers is the offensive line. The unit lost Rasheed Walker and Elgton Jenkins a season after ranking 25th in PFF’s pass-blocking grades. Romeo Doubs, Dontayvion Wicks and Emmanuel Wilson all departed as well. It leaves Jayden Reed, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson to try and exploit a strong defense. If you go back two seasons, Green Bay never produced much offensively until the game was out of reach. The Packers lost 31-29 in Week 4, but won the fourth quarter 22-3. Then they fell 27-25 in Minnesota, but won the fourth quarter 15-0. Those performances also came with superior skill players and a better offensive line compared to this matchup. Ultimately, Green Bay possesses the worst unit on the field in a Parsons-less defense. Without a coherent pass rush, I foresee Kevin O’Connell finding ways to exploit a weak corner group. Those factors lead me to predict the Vikings start the season with a home victory. Bengals vs Buccaneers Prediction: Total Under 51 Points (-125) Based on Todd Bowles’ blitzing tendencies and the Bengals’ misleading defensive record late last year, my Bengals vs Buccaneers prediction is the Total Under 51 Points (-125) . Virtually no outcome would surprise me in this game. Both teams possess advantages against the other – it just depends which ones actually play out on the field. Let’s start with the Bengals offense. If you’re Cincinnati, the concern here is that Joe Burrow faced minimal snaps against blitz-heavy teams last year. Bowles blitzed at a 30.7% rate in 2025, the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. When the Bucs didn’t blitz, the defense generated pressure at the league’s 17th-highest rate. Tampa Bay used draft picks and free agency to try and bolster the pass rush. It’ll have to work to force quick throws as it’s my belief Cincy’s receivers pose a mismatch for Tampa’s corners. However, Vea poses a massive challenge for a weak Bengals interior. Both he and first-round pick Ruben Bain Jr. could pose problems for the entire offensive line. If the Bucs force Burrow into short throws, it likely leads to fewer chunk plays that correlate with a high-scoring game. Where I’m more confident is the Bengals defense doing enough to keep Tampa’s offense at bay. While the Bucs’ offensive line remains amongst the best in the league, clear weaknesses exist. Those shortcomings sit along the interior, which will face Dexter Lawrence. How they’ll cope with that matchup remains to be seen, but it’s a nightmare on paper. That’s even before we get to the fact Tampa Bay lost Mike Evans in free agency. Additionally, Cincinnati posted decent defensive metrics toward the end of last season. Early in the year, the Bengals played terribly. But against good opponents in Weeks 12-17, they played serviceably. Over that timespan, the Bengals ranked 25th in EPA per play and 16th in success rate. Those games include three of nine opponent touchdowns via defense or special teams. Broaden the sample to include games against Pittsburgh and Cleveland at each end and the figure rises to seven of nine touchdowns. Eagles vs Commanders Prediction: Commanders Under 19.5 Points (+100) Based on Washington’s lack of continuity at offensive coordinator and the Eagles’ defensive strength, my Eagles vs Commanders prediction is the Commanders Under 19.5 Points (+100) . Laremy Tunsil is likely done for the season. Outside Jayden Daniels, Washington is relying on an aging skill group to take on one of 2025’s top defensive units. Philadelphia finished seventh in defensive DVOA last season, their second under DC Vic Fangio. En route to a Super Bowl win in 2024, the Eagles led the NFL. Late last year, the Eagles kept much better offenses under this number. Green Bay scored seven points. The Lions and Bills both stayed under 12.5 points. Washington started backups in both games against the Eagles last year. Even with Daniels available, we’ve seen the Commanders struggle in a hostile environment. Albeit on short rest, Washington scored 18 on TNF two years ago at Lincoln Financial Field. More worrisome is how Washington gets the ball back from Philadelphia to score points. The defense has consistently ranked amongst the league’s worst. Minimal changes occurred this offseason to expect an uptick in quality. Irrespective of quarterback, Washington has yet to provide a solution for Saquon Barkley. Add in some line movement on the full game over/under, and I predict the Eagles keep their rivals under a low benchmark. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . Vikings @ Buccaneers The Vikings are 2-0 after beating the Packers in Week 1 and the Bears in Week 2. Did you hear the Bears have the best offense in the NFL? Well, not after they played the Vikings, who limited them to only three points in a game where the Bears made a ton of mistakes. Chicago went 0-3 in the red zone with a costly fumble late in the game. Now the 2-0 Vikings — who, by the way, look unstoppable — head to the lowly Bucs, who are 0-2 after losses to the Bengals and Browns. The Bucs might be bad. They are older. Baker Mayfield doesn’t look great. They have a new offensive coordinator, and it looks disjointed at times on that side of the ball. Can Baker Mayfield lead his Bucs to a win in Week 3? (Getty Images) However, this is the perfect spot to wager on them. All the players and staff know what happens if they go to 0-3. The season is done. Since the NFL expanded to 14 playoff teams in 2020, only a single team has made the playoffs after starting 0-3, and it won’t be the Bucs if it does happen. The Vikings have Kyler Murray returning to the lineup, and he played only a few snaps before getting hurt. I wonder how crisp he’s going to be in his first real time on the field with this offense. This just feels like a classic NFL spot where the 0-2 team makes it happen against the 2-0 team who’s playing well. Schwartz's Pick: Buccaneers +1.5 Titans @ Giants Give me the Under in this game featuring Jameis Winston at quarterback for the Giants and a poor Titans offense on the other side of the field. Add in the potential rain and wind from a storm and scoring in MetLife Stadium feels unlikely. Winston’s arm looked dead in this appearance against the Rams on Monday night after Jaxson Dart went out. And that was Winston being healthy and in perfect condition. Now it’s outside in the wind. The Tennessee defense has been middle of the pack this season and should be able to stop a Winston-led offense. Giants' receiver Malik Nabers got beat up against the Rams, but he did return to the game. Is he completely healthy for this team? Left tackle Andrew Thomas is beat up also. The Giants offense could have a long road ahead. (Getty Images) I don’t like the Giants' offense in his game. New York's defensive line, on the other hand, should torture the Titans' offensive line. It is going to force Cam Ward into mistakes and make him uncomfortable. The Titans are only 26th in yards per play, and they scored 10 points against the Jets in Week 1 and only 20 against Philly. It’s worth mentioning they scored one of the touchdowns last weekend after a 90-yard interception return gave the offense the ball on the 10. This time, though, we're focusing strictly on spreads and totals. We've narrowed this week's card down to three wagers that stand out thanks to favorable matchups and recent trends, highlighted by a West Division showdown in Edmonton, an East Division rivalry expected to produce points and a clash between two playoff hopefuls in Vancouver. 2026 CFL Week 12: Best Bets, Picks and Predictions * All odds from 2:30 p.m. ET on Thursday, August 20, 2026. Winnipeg Blue Bombers vs. Edmonton Elks Winnipeg +4.5, -105 @ BetMGM Edmonton has been one of the CFL's biggest surprises this season, but this spread feels a bit too generous toward the home side. The Blue Bombers have had extra time to regroup following last week's victory over Ottawa and remain one of the league's most disciplined teams on both sides of the football. Winnipeg's defense has consistently limited explosive plays, which is critical against an Edmonton offense led by Cody Fajardo that thrives on sustaining long drives. For what it's worth, the Blue Bombers have allowed the fourth-most yards per game in 2026, and they'll be facing an Edmonton team that has generated the third-most yards on offense. Even if the Elks ultimately protect home field, Winnipeg has the experience and defensive playmakers to keep this game within one possession, not to mention an offense led by star-caliber players such as Zach Collaros and Brady Oliveira . Back the Blue Bombers to cover in this case. Hamilton Tiger-Cats vs. Toronto Argonauts Under 59.5 points, -105 @ FanDuel This matchup has all the ingredients of a shootout, but the total set at nearly 60 points simply looks too high here. Sure, Hamilton is coming off an emotional comeback victory over Saskatchewan, while Toronto returns home looking to bounce back after a lopsided defeat. And yes, both offenses possess enough firepower to move the ball consistently, and neither defense has been particularly reliable at preventing explosive plays throughout the season. However, the Tiger-Cats are averaging just 23.7 points per game this season, the second-worst mark in the CFL, and they've been forced to improvise under center due to the absence of Bo Levi Mitchell (ankle), while star wideout Shemar Bridges (hip) has yet to play in 2026. The Argos are favorites and tend to respond well at home after losses, but don't expect this game to be a shootout. Neither team averages more than 29.5 points per game this season, so a total above 60 points seems out of reach. Saskatchewan Roughriders vs. BC Lions Saskatchewan +1.5, -105 @ BetMGM Getting points with Saskatchewan is difficult to pass up, even on the road. The Roughriders remain one of the CFL's most complete teams when Trevor Harris is protected, and their balanced offensive attack prevents defenses from focusing on any one playmaker. While the Lions have shown flashes offensively, especially now that Nathan Rourke is back under center, the reality is that the team has struggled to consistently put together four-quarter performances, leaving the door open for Saskatchewan to capitalize. The Roughriders also possess one of the league's more physical defenses, a unit capable of generating pressure without excessive blitzing and forcing opponents into difficult second-and-long situations. While the Lions lead the CFL in yards allowed per game by a wide margin (339.6), it's hard to see their defense controlling the game against Saskatchewan's elite offense.
